purpose: Assess ASVS V7 Session Management across both session paths, and add the NO_RUNTIME_CALLER condition that was owed after a decision note credited a control nothing invokes.
requiredInvariants: Every decision resting on session invalidation names both session paths, so a divergence between them surfaces as a rejected decision rather than a stale PASS.
A control that nothing invokes is never recorded as a control; NO_RUNTIME_CALLER makes that machine-checkable.
A behavioural accident is never recorded as a control.
Where a control exists but guards something other than what the requirement asks about, it is credited and the gap is scoped.
FAIL is recorded and reported, never resolved by editing product logic.
No product logic, dependency, production, REG.RU, DNS or database change.
acceptance: NO_RUNTIME_CALLER holds when a symbol is referenced only by its own module and tests, and stops holding on the first real caller.
The V2.3.5 note is re-anchored on that condition instead of prose, discharging the debt named when it was corrected.
All 19 V7 requirements are decided: 9 PASS, 10 FAIL.
V7.2.1, V7.4.1, V7.4.2 and V7.4.3 rest on conditions naming both session paths.
V7.4.4 is FAIL, not a scoped PASS, because only one of several authenticated shells was proven.
V7.5.1 and V7.5.3 credit the wired fresh-MFA gate and scope the gap to where it is not applied.
V7.6.x are decided as applicable on the relying-party path, never as non-applicable.
The concurrent-scope guard accepts exactly the four authorized paths.
